content: 1. Avoid using venetoclax with moderate CYP3A inhibitors, or consider alternative medications. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50%. Monitor closely for signs of venetoclax toxicities. 2. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Aprepitant significantly increases the levels of vilazodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If intolerable adverse effects occur with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the daily dose of vilazodone to 20 mg. 4. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of vinblastine, vincristine, liposomal vincristine, and vinorelbine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions are considered minor, and their clinical significance is unknown. 5. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 6. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Aprepitant decreases the levels or effects of warfarin by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. For patients on chronic warfarin therapy, monitor INR closely during the two-week period following aprepitant or fosaprepitant administration, particularly at 7–10 days after administration with each chemotherapy cycle. 8. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of zaleplon, zanubrutinib, ziprasidone, zolpidem, and zonisamide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions are considered minor, and their clinical significance is unknown. For zanubrutinib, reduce the dose when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Interrupt the dose as recommended for adverse reactions, and resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. Refer to zanubrutinib dosage modifications for precise recommendations. 10. Aprepitant is generally comparable to standard treatments for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) and to ondansetron for postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV). 11. Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders associated with aprepitant include pruritus, rash, urticaria, and rare cases of Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis. 12. Immune system disorders include hypersensitivity reactions, including rare anaphylactic reactions. 13. Nervous system disorders include reports of ifosfamide-induced neurotoxicity when co-administered with aprepitant. 14. Avoid concomitant use of aprepitant with pimozide due to the risk of serious interactions. 15. There is insufficient data on the use of aprepitant in pregnant women to determine drug-associated risks. Avoid aprepitant IV emulsion in pregnant women due to its alcohol content. 16. Aprepitant may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Advise females of reproductive potential using hormonal contraceptives to use effective alternative or backup non-hormonal contraceptive methods (e.g., condoms or spermicides) during treatment and for one month following the last dose of aprepitant. 17. It is unknown whether aprepitant is excreted in human milk. A decision should be made to discontinue nursing or discontinue the drug, considering the importance of the drug to the mother. 18. Aprepitant is a selective, high-affinity antagonist of human substance P/neurokinin 1 (NK1) receptors. It has little or no affinity for serotonin (5-HT3), dopamine, or corticosteroid receptors. 19. In animal models, aprepitant inhibits emesis induced by cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents, such as cisplatin, via central actions. Animal and human studies have shown that aprepitant augments the antiemetic activity of the 5-HT3 receptor antagonist ondansetron and the corticosteroid dexamethasone, inhibiting both the acute and delayed phases of cisplatin-induced emesis. 20. Aprepitant has an oral bioavailability of 60–65%, is highly protein-bound (>95%), and has a volume of distribution of 70 L. It crosses the blood-brain barrier in humans. 21. Aprepitant is metabolized primarily by hepatic CYP3A4, with minor contributions from CYP1A2 and CYP2C19. It inhibits CYP3A4 and induces CYP2C9. Its half-life is 9–13 hours, and total body clearance is 62–90 mL/min. Excretion following IV administration is 57% via urine and 45% via feces. It is not dialyzable. 22. Inspect the vial for particulate matter and discoloration before administration. Discard if present. The emulsion should appear opaque and off-white to amber in color. 23. Aprepitant capsules should be swallowed whole and can be taken with or without food. Store capsules at room temperature (20–25°C or 68–77°F). Liquid formulations should be refrigerated and discarded after 72 hours. Do not freeze. When ready to use, the liquid form may be stored at room temperature for up to 3 hours. 24. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard expired or unused products. 25. Aprepitant is used with other medications to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by cancer chemotherapy. It does not treat nausea or vomiting that has already started. 26. Common side effects include tiredness and hiccups. Serious allergic reactions are rare. Always consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. 27. Before taking aprepitant, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, fosaprepitant, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. 28. During pregnancy, aprepitant should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. 29. Drug interactions may alter how aprepitant or other medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Examples of interacting drugs include azole antifungals (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole), diltiazem, macrolide antibiotics (e.g., clarithromycin, erythromycin), nefazodone, HIV protease inhibitors (e.g., nelfinavir), rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), ritonavir, and St. John’s wort. 30. Aprepitant can either speed up or slow down the removal of other medications from the body, potentially affecting their efficacy. For example, aprepitant may affect the effectiveness of warfarin and hormonal birth control methods (e.g., pills, patches, or rings). Discuss reliable backup birth control methods with your doctor while using this medication and for one month after the last dose. 31. In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. In the U.S., call 911 or the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. 32. If a dose is missed, consult your doctor or pharmacist for a new dosing schedule. 33. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about aprepitant. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
